Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=10|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Oasahiko-jinja, otorii-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]] '''Oasahiko Shrine'' (Oasahiko Shrine) is located in {{ill|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|WD=Q160734|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Naruto City|Q460812|WD=Q460812|1=Naruto, Tokushima}}{{ill|lt=Cannabis Town Bando|Q11442044|WD=Q11442044|1=Ōasa-chō Bandō}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinai Shrine|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|lt=Meishin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}}), {{ill|lt=Awakuni|Q907457|WD=Q907457|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}{{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. {{ill|lt=Modern shrine rank system|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=old shrine rank|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and currently it is {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}.He is also commonly known as ``Kannabi-san,'' and is worshiped as the guardian deity of both Awa and {{ill|lt=Awaji province|Q1053717|WD=Q1053717|1=Awaji Province}} countries, and currently the guardian deity of Tokushima Prefecture. The precincts are designated as {{ill|lt=Kannabiyama Prefectural Natural Park|Q8081421|WD=Q8081421|1=Ōasayama Prefectural Natural Park}}. === Enshrined God === ; Main enshrined deity * Cannabihikojin - The son of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenhiwashi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, and considered to be the ancestor of the Awaimbe clan. ; Deity enshrined * {{ill|lt=Sartahiko|Q3090037|WD=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko Okami|1=Sarutahiko Ōkami}} - It has been enshrined at {{ill|lt=Mt. Cannabis_(Tokushima Prefecture)|Q11442028|WD=Q11442028|lt=Mt. Cannabis|1=Mount Ōasa}} since ancient times, and is said to have been later enshrined there.From "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" (hereinafter referred to as "Japanese Gods") Kenichi Tanikawa (ed.) "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" Hakusuisha Co., Ltd. October 1984. According to , in ancient times, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami, as stated in "{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Chronicle|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}", which was established in {{ill|lt=Muromachi period|Q334845|WD=Q334845|1=Muromachi period}}, and {{ill|lt=culture (era name)|Q1373146|WD=Q1373146|lt=Bunka|1=Bunka}} As can be seen in the ``Awa Koku Shikisha Ryakko'' written in 1815|Q6948}}, it is said that the {{ill|lt=Urabe clan|Q11409028|WD=Q11409028|lt=Urabe|1=Urabe clan}} line of thought is generally unified in Sarutahiko Okami. In "Japanese Gods," on the other hand, on the side of shrines and priests, {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}}14 ({{ill|lt=1729|Q6952|WD=Q6952|1=1729}}) and {{jal ink|Horeki|Q1194397}} In the 4th year ({{ill|lt=1754|Q7623|WD=Q7623|1=1754}}), the district magistrate said, ``The ritual of worshiping Sarutahiko Omikami, which is the object of worship. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|lt=Tenhi Washi God|Q10939697|WD=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto|1=Otori-sama}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|lt=Ibe clan|Q8189229|WD=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan|1=Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|lt=Kogo Shui|Q531555|WD=Q531555|1=Kogo Shūi}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|lt=casinoki|Q389185|WD=Q389185|lt=grain|1=Paper mulberry}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp|1=UNKNOWN}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|lt=Awa Province|Q1053044|WD=Q1053044|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto. {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|lt=Ibe Shrine|Q11490722|WD=Q11490722|1=Inbe Shrine}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami|1=UNKNOWN}}, who accompanied {{ill|lt=Tensonkō|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|lt=Kunitsukami|Q609|WD=Q609|ltq=Q609|1=Kateri Tekakwitha}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows. According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|lt=Koshin belief|Q3082157|WD=Q3082157|1=Kōshin}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period. === History === According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo|1=UNKNOWN}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province. "{{ill|lt=Japan's Three Dynasty Chronicles|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}" {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}} According to the article dated January 27, 1997 ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}}), our company has been conferred the rank of {{ill|lt=Divine Rank|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025|1=Shinkai (divine rank)}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Upper|1=UNKNOWN}}. According to an article in "Nihon Sandai Jiroku", our company further states that in the article dated April 23, 9th year of Jogan ({{ill|lt=867|Q30347|WD=Q30347|1=867}}), ink|878|Q23910}}) In the article of April 14th, he advanced to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in the article of November 1st, Genkei 7 ({{ill|lt=883|Q30355|WD=Q30355|1=883}}), he advanced to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Upper|1=UNKNOWN}}. In {{ill|lt=Extension (Era Name)|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|lt=Extension|1=Enchō}}5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), it was promoted to Shikinai-sha and Meishin-taisha Shrine according to the ``{{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}''.From the {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}} to the {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|WD=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}, {{ill|lt=Jinguji|Q1074971|WD=Q1074971|1=Jingū-ji}}, which essentially operated shrines based on the {{ill|lt=syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism|Q2279088|WD=Q2279088|1=Shinbutsu-shūgō}} philosophy, were established in various places, but ``Shokoku Ichi no Miya'' Koichiro Irie "Shokoku Ichi no Miya" Mobile Classroom Publishing Department June 2001. states that the first temple {{ill|lt=Ryozenji (Naruto City)|Q1085463|WD=Q1085463|lt=Ryozenji|1=Ryōzen-ji (Naruto)}} of {{ill|lt=88 temples in Shikoku|Q1972399|WD=Q1972399|1=Shikoku Pilgrimage}} was our Jingu temple. However, from "Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries" edited by the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries Research Group, "Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries", Iwata Shoin Co., Ltd., February 2000. states that {{ill|lt=Bettoji Temple|Q11396755|WD=Q11396755|1=Bettō-ji}} is unknown. 『{{ill|lt=Gunjo Asano|Q11517735|WD=Q11517735|1=Chōya Gunsai}} In Volume 6, there is a message that the god of cannabis in Awa Province was cursed due to excessive impurity in the rituals, so a messenger should be sent to perform a mid-purification and purify the people. There is a {{ill|lt=jingikan|Q2264720|WD=Q2264720|1=Department of Divinities}} sojo dated June 10, 743}}4 ({{ill|lt=1080|Q19448|WD=Q19448|1=1080}}).Although our company is listed as Ichinomiya in Awa Province in the ``Dainihonkoku Ichinomiya'', which is said to have been established during the Muromachi period, in ``Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries'' , (Japan)|Q264012|During the Nanbokucho era}}, our company boasted a traditional shrine status and was close to the guardian post of the {{ill|lt=Hosokawa clan#Awa guardian family (Sanshu family)|Q2736120|WD=Q2736120|lt=Hosokawa clan|1=Hosokawa clan}}. (Tokushima City)|Q11352598|Ichinomiya Shrine}} It is considered that it has been given the status of a new Ichinomiya shrine in Awa Province. "Visiting the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation" Edited by the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation Official guidebook "Visiting the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation" by the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation From December 2008. According to , it was protected by the Hosokawa clan and the {{ill|lt=Miyoshi clan|Q2975329|WD=Q2975329|1=Miyoshi clan}} during the Muromachi period, and by the {{ill|lt=Tokushima clan|Q3034557|WD=Q3034557|1=Tokushima Domain}} lord {{ill|lt=Hachisuka clan|Q2975261|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka family|1=Hachisuka clan}} during the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}. In addition, in the 4th year of Kyoho ({{ill|lt=1719|Q6902|WD=Q6902|1=1719}}), the highest divine rank of {{ill|lt=Shoichii|Q11123258|WD=Q11123258|1=Senior First Rank}} was conferred. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}6 ({{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757|1=1873}}), it was promoted to Kokuheichusha, and in Meiji 13 ({{ill|lt=1880|Q7806|WD=Q7806|1=1880}}), the main hall and the rest were built using national funds.In {{ill|lt=Taisho|Q329174|WD=Q329174|1=Taishō era}}8 ({{ill|lt=1919|Q2157|WD=Q2157|1=1919}}), a stone arch bridge was completed behind the main shrine. This bridge is called {{ill|lt=German Bridge|Q11322494|WD=Q11322494|1=German Bridge}} because it was built based on the proposal and construction of German soldiers who had been imprisoned in {{ill|lt=Bando POW camp|Q324270|WD=Q324270|1=Bandō prisoner-of-war camp}} as prisoners of war during {{ill|lt=World War I|Q361|WD=Q361|1=World War I}} when they returned home. After the {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Old Shrine Ranking|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was abolished after {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=World War II|1=UNKNOWN}}, it became {{ill|lt=Bepped Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}}, which was encompassed by {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. In {{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}45 ({{ill|lt=1970|Q2474|WD=Q2474|1=1970}}), the Oratory Hall, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inner Worship Hall|1=UNKNOWN}}, and Outer Worship Hall were built with donations from worshipers. === Precincts === [[File:Oasahiko-jinja, honden-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|main hall}}]] [[File:Oasahiko-jinja, kusu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Oasahiko-jinja (Naruto City designated natural monument)}}]] * Main shrine - Rebuilt with national funds in 1880. * Inner worship hall and outer worship hall - Rebuilt in 1970. * Noritoden - Rebuilt in 1970. * Kojin Sapporo * Jinko * Shinbasha * Shrine office * Awarding place * Okumiya Aihaisho * Sanshuden * {{ill|lt=campus|UNKNOWN|lt=large camphor}} - A sacred tree said to be over 1000 years old. Designated by Naruto City {{ill|lt=natural monument|Q23790|WD=Q23790|1=Natural monument}}. * German Bridge - See "{{ill|lt=Deutsche Bridge|Q11322494|WD=Q11322494|1=German Bridge}}". * Megane Bridge - Built by German soldiers who were imprisoned in {{ill|lt=Bando POW camp|Q324270|WD=Q324270|1=Bandō prisoner-of-war camp}} during the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Taisho period|1=UNKNOWN}}. * Otorii - You can see it when you pass by {{ill|lt=Reizanji (Naruto City)|Q1085463|WD=Q1085463|lt=Reizanji|1=Ryōzen-ji (Naruto)}} and go under the elevated {{ill|lt=Takamatsu Expressway|Q7677132|WD=Q7677132|1=Takamatsu Expressway}}. From here, a path lined with pine trees continues for about 800 meters. Rebuilt with steel pipes in 2002. Height: 14.6m. * Okumiyamine Shrine - Enshrined at the top of Mt. Oasayama at an altitude of 538m. Climbing for about an hour and a half. '''Precincts end shrine''' * Nishinomiyasha * Water Shrine * Chugusha * Yama Shrine * Toyoukesha * Maruyama Inari Shrine * Maruyamasha * Tenjin Shrine * No Shrine File:Oasahiko-jinja, Chugusha.jpg|Chugusha File:Oasahiko-jinja, Yama-jinja.jpg|Yama Shrine File:Oasahiko-jinja, Toyoukesha.jpg|Toyoukesha File:Oasahiko-jinja, Ten-jinja.jpg|Tenjin Shrine File:Oasahiko-jinja, No-jinja.jpg|No Shrine === Cultural assets === === Tokushima Prefecture designated cultural property === * Historic sites ** {{ill|lt=German Bridge|Q11322494|WD=Q11322494|1=German Bridge}}[https://www.city.naruto.tokushima.jp/manabu/bunka/bunkazai/ken_shitei/10_doitsu-bashi.html Historic Site German Bridge] (Naruto City homepage). === Naruto City designated cultural property === * Natural monument ** Camphor tree at Cannabis Hiko Shrine [https://www.city.naruto.tokushima.jp/manabu/bunka/bunkazai/shi_shitei/52_ooasahikojinja-kusunoki.html Natural monument Camphor tree at Cannabis Hiko Shrine] (Naruto City homepage). - A large camphor tree that is said to be over a thousand years old. === Transportation access === {{Location map+|Japan Tokushima|width=260|caption='''Kannabihiko Shrine''' location|float=right|places= {{Location map~|Japan Tokushima|lat_deg=34|lat_min=10|lat_sec=15.34|lon_deg=134|lon_min=30|lon_sec=9.24|position=left|label='''Kannabihiko Shrine'''|label_size=105}} {{Location map~|Japan Tokushima|lat_deg=34|lat_min=4|lat_sec=13|lon_deg=134|lon_min=33|lon_sec=17.8|position=right|mark=blue pog.svg|label=Tokushima City}}}} * Nearest bus stop: {{ill|lt=Tokushima Bus|Q11489648|WD=Q11489648|1=Tokushima Bus}} 20 minutes walk from Reizanji-mae on the Naruto Cannabi Line. * Nearest express bus stop: {{ill|lt=Takamatsu Expressway|Q7677132|WD=Q7677132|1=Takamatsu Expressway}} 8 minutes walk from {{ill|lt=Naruto Nishi Parking Area|Q11173862|WD=Q11173862|lt=Naruto Nishi Bus Stop|1=Naruto-nishi parking area}}. * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Shikoku Railway|Q496531|WD=Q496531|lt=JR Shikoku|1=Shikoku Railway Company}}{{ill|lt=Kotoku Line|Q859984|WD=Q859984|1=Kōtoku Line}} {{ill|lt=Bando Station|Q4854805|WD=Q4854805|1=Bandō Station}} (about 25 minutes walk) === Surroundings === * {{ill|lt=Naruto City Kagawa Toyohiko Memorial Hall|Q17209243|WD=Q17209243|1=Naruto City Kagawa Toyohiko Memorial Museum}} - 4 minutes walk. * {{ill|lt=Roadside Station 9th Village|Q11641439|WD=Q11641439|1=Roadside station Dai9-no-sato}} - 5 minutes walk. * {{ill|lt=Naruto City German Pavilion|Q3740674|WD=Q3740674|1=Naruto German House}} - 6 minutes walk. * {{ill|lt=German Village Park|Q65240999|WD=Q65240999|1=German Village Park}} - 10 minutes walk. The site of {{ill|lt=Bando POW camp|Q324270|WD=Q324270|1=Bandō prisoner-of-war camp}}. * {{ill|lt=Awa Taisho Roman Baltic Garden|Q11657519|WD=Q11657519|1=Baruto-no-niwa}} - 12 minutes walk. {{ill|lt=Museum|Q33506|WD=Q33506|1=Museum}} and {{ill|lt=Theme Park|Q2416723|WD=Q2416723|1=Theme park}}, where the location set of the movie "{{ill|lt=Baltic Paradise|Q690615|WD=Q690615|1=Baruto no Gakuen}}" and the actual Bando POW camp barracks were relocated. * {{ill|lt=Ryozenji Temple (Naruto City)|Q1085463|WD=Q1085463|lt=Ryozenji Temple|1=Ryōzen-ji (Naruto)}} - 12 minutes walk. {{ill|lt=88 Shikoku Sites|Q1972399|WD=Q1972399|1=Shikoku Pilgrimage}} No. 1 Sacred Site === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} === References === * {{ill|lt=Kokushi Taikei|Q3894478|WD=Q3894478|1=Katsumi Kuroita}} Edited by Kokushi Taikei Compilation Association “{{ill|lt=Kokushi Taikei|Q10926780|WD=Q10926780|lt=Kokushi Taikei|1=Kokushi Taikei}} Volume 29 {{ill|lt=Asano gun publication|Q11517735|WD=Q11517735|1=Chōya Gunsai}}” {{ill|lt=Yoshikawa Kobunkan|Q4346755|WD=Q4346755|lt=Yoshikawa Kobunkan Co., Ltd.|1=Yoshikawa Kōbunkan}} November 1964 * Edited by Katsumi Kuroita, Kokushi Taikei Editorial Committee, “Kokushi Taikei Volume 4 {{ill|lt=Answers of Three Japanese Dynasties|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}” Yoshikawa Kobunkan Co., Ltd. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|lt=Tenhi Washi God|Q10939697|WD=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto|1=Otori-sama}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|lt=Ibe clan|Q8189229|WD=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan|1=Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|lt=Kogo Shui|Q531555|WD=Q531555|1=Kogo Shūi}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|lt=casinoki|Q389185|WD=Q389185|lt=grain|1=Paper mulberry}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp|1=UNKNOWN}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|lt=Awa Province|Q1053044|WD=Q1053044|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto. {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|lt=Ibe Shrine|Q11490722|WD=Q11490722|1=Inbe Shrine}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami|1=UNKNOWN}}, who accompanied {{ill|lt=Tensonkō|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|lt=Kunitsukami|Q609|WD=Q609|ltq=Q609|1=Kateri Tekakwitha}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows. According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|lt=Koshin belief|Q3082157|WD=Q3082157|1=Kōshin}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period. === History === According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo|1=UNKNOWN}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province. "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" Hakusuisha Co., Ltd. October 1984. According to , in ancient times, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami, as stated in "{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Chronicle|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}", which was established in {{ill|lt=Muromachi period|Q334845|WD=Q334845|1=Muromachi period}}, and {{ill|lt=culture (era name)|Q1373146|WD=Q1373146|lt=Bunka|1=Bunka}} As can be seen in the ``Awa Koku Shikisha Ryakko'' written in 1815|Q6948}}, it is said that the {{ill|lt=Urabe clan|Q11409028|WD=Q11409028|lt=Urabe|1=Urabe clan}} line of thought is generally unified in Sarutahiko Okami. In "Japanese Gods," on the other hand, on the side of shrines and priests, {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}}14 ({{ill|lt=1729|Q6952|WD=Q6952|1=1729}}) and {{jal ink|Horeki|Q1194397}} In the 4th year ({{ill|lt=1754|Q7623|WD=Q7623|1=1754}}), the district magistrate said, ``The ritual of worshiping Sarutahiko Omikami, which is the object of worship. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|lt=Tenhi Washi God|Q10939697|WD=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto|1=Otori-sama}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|lt=Ibe clan|Q8189229|WD=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan|1=Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|lt=Kogo Shui|Q531555|WD=Q531555|1=Kogo Shūi}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|lt=casinoki|Q389185|WD=Q389185|lt=grain|1=Paper mulberry}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp|1=UNKNOWN}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|lt=Awa Province|Q1053044|WD=Q1053044|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto. {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|lt=Ibe Shrine|Q11490722|WD=Q11490722|1=Inbe Shrine}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami|1=UNKNOWN}}, who accompanied {{ill|lt=Tensonkō|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|lt=Kunitsukami|Q609|WD=Q609|ltq=Q609|1=Kateri Tekakwitha}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows. According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|lt=Koshin belief|Q3082157|WD=Q3082157|1=Kōshin}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period. === History === According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo|1=UNKNOWN}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province. "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" Hakusuisha Co., Ltd. October 1984. According to , in ancient times, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami, as stated in "{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Chronicle|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}", which was established in {{ill|lt=Muromachi period|Q334845|WD=Q334845|1=Muromachi period}}, and {{ill|lt=culture (era name)|Q1373146|WD=Q1373146|lt=Bunka|1=Bunka}} As can be seen in the ``Awa Koku Shikisha Ryakko'' written in 1815|Q6948}}, it is said that the {{ill|lt=Urabe clan|Q11409028|WD=Q11409028|lt=Urabe|1=Urabe clan}} line of thought is generally unified in Sarutahiko Okami. In "Japanese Gods," on the other hand, on the side of shrines and priests, {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}}14 ({{ill|lt=1729|Q6952|WD=Q6952|1=1729}}) and {{jal ink|Horeki|Q1194397}} In the 4th year ({{ill|lt=1754|Q7623|WD=Q7623|1=1754}}), the district magistrate said, ``The ritual of worshiping Sarutahiko Omikami, which is the object of worship. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|lt=Tenhi Washi God|Q10939697|WD=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto|1=Otori-sama}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|lt=Ibe clan|Q8189229|WD=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan|1=Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|lt=Kogo Shui|Q531555|WD=Q531555|1=Kogo Shūi}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|lt=casinoki|Q389185|WD=Q389185|lt=grain|1=Paper mulberry}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp|1=UNKNOWN}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|lt=Awa Province|Q1053044|WD=Q1053044|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto. {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|lt=Ibe Shrine|Q11490722|WD=Q11490722|1=Inbe Shrine}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami|1=UNKNOWN}}, who accompanied {{ill|lt=Tensonkō|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|lt=Kunitsukami|Q609|WD=Q609|ltq=Q609|1=Kateri Tekakwitha}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows. According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|lt=Koshin belief|Q3082157|WD=Q3082157|1=Kōshin}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period. === History === According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo|1=UNKNOWN}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province. The precincts are designated as {{ill|lt=Kannabiyama Prefectural Natural Park|Q8081421|WD=Q8081421|1=Ōasayama Prefectural Natural Park}}. === Enshrined God === ; Main enshrined deity * Cannabihikojin - The son of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenhiwashi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, and considered to be the ancestor of the Awaimbe clan. ; Deity enshrined * {{ill|lt=Sartahiko|Q3090037|WD=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko Okami|1=Sarutahiko Ōkami}} - It has been enshrined at {{ill|lt=Mt. Cannabis_(Tokushima Prefecture)|Q11442028|WD=Q11442028|lt=Mt. Cannabis|1=Mount Ōasa}} since ancient times, and is said to have been later enshrined there.From "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" (hereinafter referred to as "Japanese Gods") Kenichi Tanikawa (ed.) "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" Hakusuisha Co., Ltd. October 1984. According to , in ancient times, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami, as stated in "{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Chronicle|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}", which was established in {{ill|lt=Muromachi period|Q334845|WD=Q334845|1=Muromachi period}}, and {{ill|lt=culture (era name)|Q1373146|WD=Q1373146|lt=Bunka|1=Bunka}} As can be seen in the ``Awa Koku Shikisha Ryakko'' written in 1815|Q6948}}, it is said that the {{ill|lt=Urabe clan|Q11409028|WD=Q11409028|lt=Urabe|1=Urabe clan}} line of thought is generally unified in Sarutahiko Okami. In "Japanese Gods," on the other hand, on the side of shrines and priests, {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}}14 ({{ill|lt=1729|Q6952|WD=Q6952|1=1729}}) and {{jal ink|Horeki|Q1194397}} In the 4th year ({{ill|lt=1754|Q7623|WD=Q7623|1=1754}}), the district magistrate said, ``The ritual of worshiping Sarutahiko Omikami, which is the object of worship. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|lt=Tenhi Washi God|Q10939697|WD=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto|1=Otori-sama}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|lt=Ibe clan|Q8189229|WD=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan|1=Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|lt=Kogo Shui|Q531555|WD=Q531555|1=Kogo Shūi}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|lt=casinoki|Q389185|WD=Q389185|lt=grain|1=Paper mulberry}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp|1=UNKNOWN}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|lt=Awa Province|Q1053044|WD=Q1053044|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto. {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|lt=Ibe Shrine|Q11490722|WD=Q11490722|1=Inbe Shrine}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami|1=UNKNOWN}}, who accompanied {{ill|lt=Tensonkō|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|lt=Kunitsukami|Q609|WD=Q609|ltq=Q609|1=Kateri Tekakwitha}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows. According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|lt=Koshin belief|Q3082157|WD=Q3082157|1=Kōshin}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period. === History === According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo|1=UNKNOWN}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province. "{{ill|lt=Japan's Three Dynasty Chronicles|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}" {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}} According to the article dated January 27, 1997 ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}}), our company has been conferred the rank of {{ill|lt=Divine Rank|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025|1=Shinkai (divine rank)}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Upper|1=UNKNOWN}}. The precincts are designated as {{ill|lt=Kannabiyama Prefectural Natural Park|Q8081421|WD=Q8081421|1=Ōasayama Prefectural Natural Park}}. === Enshrined God === ; Main enshrined deity * Cannabihikojin - The son of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenhiwashi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, and considered to be the ancestor of the Awaimbe clan. ; Deity enshrined * {{ill|lt=Sartahiko|Q3090037|WD=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko Okami|1=Sarutahiko Ōkami}} - It has been enshrined at {{ill|lt=Mt. Cannabis_(Tokushima Prefecture)|Q11442028|WD=Q11442028|lt=Mt. Cannabis|1=Mount Ōasa}} since ancient times, and is said to have been later enshrined there.From "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" (hereinafter referred to as "Japanese Gods") Kenichi Tanikawa (ed.) "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" Hakusuisha Co., Ltd. October 1984. According to , in ancient times, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami, as stated in "{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Chronicle|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}", which was established in {{ill|lt=Muromachi period|Q334845|WD=Q334845|1=Muromachi period}}, and {{ill|lt=culture (era name)|Q1373146|WD=Q1373146|lt=Bunka|1=Bunka}} As can be seen in the ``Awa Koku Shikisha Ryakko'' written in 1815|Q6948}}, it is said that the {{ill|lt=Urabe clan|Q11409028|WD=Q11409028|lt=Urabe|1=Urabe clan}} line of thought is generally unified in Sarutahiko Okami. In "Japanese Gods," on the other hand, on the side of shrines and priests, {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}}14 ({{ill|lt=1729|Q6952|WD=Q6952|1=1729}}) and {{jal ink|Horeki|Q1194397}} In the 4th year ({{ill|lt=1754|Q7623|WD=Q7623|1=1754}}), the district magistrate said, ``The ritual of worshiping Sarutahiko Omikami, which is the object of worship. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|lt=Tenhi Washi God|Q10939697|WD=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto|1=Otori-sama}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|lt=Ibe clan|Q8189229|WD=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan|1=Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|lt=Kogo Shui|Q531555|WD=Q531555|1=Kogo Shūi}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|lt=casinoki|Q389185|WD=Q389185|lt=grain|1=Paper mulberry}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp|1=UNKNOWN}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|lt=Awa Province|Q1053044|WD=Q1053044|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto. {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|lt=Ibe Shrine|Q11490722|WD=Q11490722|1=Inbe Shrine}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami|1=UNKNOWN}}, who accompanied {{ill|lt=Tensonkō|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|lt=Kunitsukami|Q609|WD=Q609|ltq=Q609|1=Kateri Tekakwitha}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows. According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|lt=Koshin belief|Q3082157|WD=Q3082157|1=Kōshin}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period. === History === According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo|1=UNKNOWN}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province. "{{ill|lt=Japan's Three Dynasty Chronicles|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}" {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}} According to the article dated January 27, 1997 ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}}), our company has been conferred the rank of {{ill|lt=Divine Rank|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025|1=Shinkai (divine rank)}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Upper|1=UNKNOWN}}. According to an article in "Nihon Sandai Jiroku", our company further states that in the article dated April 23, 9th year of Jogan ({{ill|lt=867|Q30347|WD=Q30347|1=867}}), ink|878|Q23910}}) In the article of April 14th, he advanced to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in the article of November 1st, Genkei 7 ({{ill|lt=883|Q30355|WD=Q30355|1=883}}), he advanced to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Upper|1=UNKNOWN}}. This bridge is called {{ill|lt=German Bridge|Q11322494|WD=Q11322494|1=German Bridge}} because it was built based on the proposal and construction of German soldiers who had been imprisoned in {{ill|lt=Bando POW camp|Q324270|WD=Q324270|1=Bandō prisoner-of-war camp}} as prisoners of war during {{ill|lt=World War I|Q361|WD=Q361|1=World War I}} when they returned home.
